status: Quantitative prioritization described; weights/formula not in SCRIPT
method: Adaptation Priorities Reports (APRs) rank exposed State Highway System assets using prioritization scores. SCRIPT says scores consider timing of climate impacts, severity/span, asset condition as sensitivity, number of users affected, and network redundancy; district/local knowledge can adjust rankings. STCAP/LTCAP project funding additionally considers recurring damage/failure risk, mobility/economy/safety benefits, community/environment/critical-infrastructure benefits, equity, and secondary GHG/VMT co-benefits.
inputs: Climate stressor exposure; impact timing; severity/span; asset condition; users affected; redundancy; equity/co-benefits for project selection.
scale: Prioritization scores/rankings; exact numeric scale not disclosed in SCRIPT.
project: Projects initially screened using APR data or Cal-Adapt; funding selection checks vulnerability, policy alignment, schedule, permitting, and equity/co-benefits.

status: Explicit quantitative formula
method: CDOT scores risk as Risk Score = T x C x V. T is threat likelihood/probability, C is consequence of impact, and V is vulnerability/probability that the estimated consequence is realized. Threats and risk scores are updated every four years with the TAMP cycle or as needed.
inputs: Threat likelihood; consequence; vulnerability. System criticality also uses AADT, redundancy, roadway classification, freight value, social vulnerability, and tourism value.
scale: T is scored 1-5; C and V use scoring rubrics referenced in Section 7.1. Product gives risk score.
project: 10-Year Plan resilience integration uses criticality GIS to identify high/medium/low criticality and focus resilience assessment on high-opportunity projects.

status: Method in development; no final scoring formula
method: CTDOT is developing a FHWA VAST-based vulnerability assessment. The plan identifies exposure, sensitivity, and adaptive capacity as the indicator types, but Step 4 Assess Vulnerability is still ongoing/refining.
inputs: Four hazards: flooding, hurricane/tropical cyclone/storm surge, extreme heat, extreme cold/winter weather; asset location, condition, characteristics, surrounding community; exposure/sensitivity/adaptive capacity.
scale: No final scoring scale or formula published in the RIP excerpt; VAST-based model under development.
project: RIP includes a PROTECT-eligible project screening process and project categories; scoring criteria are not finalized in the downloaded plan.

status: Weighted matrix plus developing quantitative risk model
method: DelDOT first used maintenance-district input to identify frequently flooded roadways, then applied a weighted prioritization matrix. It is moving to quantitative annual-risk modeling for bridges and pavement vulnerable to rainfall and sunny-day flooding.
inputs: Frequently flooded roadway history; flood datasets; traffic/infrastructure; community factors; owner costs; user costs; threat probabilities such as embankment erodibility, roadway flooding, bridge flooding, debris potential.
scale: Frequently Flooded Roadways matrix: Flood History 50 pts; Flood Data 25 pts; Infrastructure/Traffic 15 pts; Community 10 pts. Subfactors are equally weighted within categories as listed. Quant model outputs risk for assets/corridors.
project: Risk model outputs feed resilience investment strategy; additional criteria include route criticality, essential facilities, equity, AADT, DTC ridership, community size, employment density, readiness, bundling, timeliness, and recent capital work.

status: No risk scoring method in downloaded file
method: Downloaded FDOT file is a Community Engagement Plan for resilience activities, not the RIP methodology. It discusses identifying vulnerabilities and resilience-related plans/projects but does not define a scoring formula.
inputs: Public/stakeholder engagement around resilience activities; vulnerability identification mentioned generally.
scale: No scoring scale found in downloaded PDF.
project: No project risk scoring method found in downloaded PDF.

status: Explicit hazard formula; project composite ranking described
method: Iowa DOT RWG prioritized natural hazards using a risk-based assessment: risk/vulnerability = likelihood x consequence. Lower likelihood values mean rare events; higher values mean higher probability. Lower consequence values mean lower transportation-system impact; higher values mean significant damage.
inputs: Hazard likelihood and consequence; later project screening uses identified vulnerabilities/hazards, PROTECT eligibility, location criticality, and cost effectiveness.
scale: Hazards grouped into three tiers by risk scores and preferred mitigation approach. Exact numeric scale for likelihood/consequence is shown in matrix/table but not fully extracted as text.
project: Annual district solicitation; two-phase screening for vulnerabilities and PROTECT eligibility; projects ranked by system criticality and cost effectiveness; composite ranking reviewed by RWG and Program Team for 5YP/STIP candidates.

status: Explicit matrix + FHWA VAST scoring
method: KYTC describes a hybrid risk-based vulnerability assessment: data analysis, district workshops, and GIS compilation. A risk matrix considers likelihood and severity/consequence. Appendix uses FHWA VAST: exposure, sensitivity, and adaptive capacity indicators produce vulnerability scores.
inputs: Likelihood 1-5; severity/consequence; exposure; sensitivity; adaptive capacity; 22 datasets for earthquake, flooding, landslide, sinkholes; workshop keypad inputs; asset criticality indicators.
scale: Likelihood is 1-5. VAST indicator scores are 1-4; exposure/sensitivity high score = more exposure/sensitivity; adaptive capacity high score = less capacity. Exposure/sensitivity/adaptive capacity default weights are 33% each; final vulnerability score is 1-4, higher = more vulnerable.
project: Assets with vulnerability score >=3.5 are highlighted by district/hazard; GIS database supports maps and project prioritization.

status: Multiple modal methods; statewide quantitative approach in progress
method: MDOT uses MDEM hazard probability ratings and modal vulnerability assessments. SHA scored roadway assets for threats such as storm surge and sea-level rise. MDOT is moving toward quantitative asset-level risk assessments using asset location, condition/design parameters, and threat likelihood.
inputs: Hazard probability; asset location; condition; design parameters; threat likelihood; Climate Change Vulnerability Viewer; FEMA FIRM; maintenance records; system redundancy, demand, social vulnerability in pilot.
scale: MDEM hazard probability rating: 1 unlikely (< once/30 years), 2 likely (< once/5 years but > once/30 years), 3 highly likely (> once/5 years). Pilot annual risk cost = owner risk from asset failure/repair + user risk from rerouting.
project: Prioritization intended to use annualized risk with social, economic, and financial impacts; FFY22-23 funds focused on implementation-ready/immediate-benefit projects.

status: Explicit weighted formula
method: Michigan calculates risk from exposure, sensitivity, and criticality. Formula: Risk = (Criticality Score x 25%) + ((Exposure x 75% + Sensitivity x 25%) x 75%). Vulnerability is the exposure/sensitivity component and contributes 75% of total risk.
inputs: Exposure; sensitivity; criticality. Criticality indicators include AADT, commercial AADT, functional class, NHS status, CEJEST disadvantaged communities. Exposure varies by hazard; sensitivity includes condition/scour/age/asset type.
scale: Each asset score is 1-4. High risk = 3-4; medium = 2-2.99; low = 1-1.99. Exposure and sensitivity tables use percentile/natural-break values and hazard-specific weights.
project: High-risk asset counts by hazard/asset type support implementation prioritization; examples include detailed factor-level scores for use cases.

status: Quantitative climate risk score; formula summarized not fully numeric
method: MnDOT combines asset-level climate hazard exposure with potential traveler impacts to create climate risk scores for roads, bridges/large culverts, and slopes.
inputs: Hazard exposure across timeframes/emissions scenarios; traveler impacts measured by federal functional classification as proxy for travelers affected; network density as proxy for redundancy/detour options.
scale: Climate risk score categories: Very Low, Low, Medium, High, Very High. Exact numeric calculation not disclosed in main text; Appendix B contains method details.
project: RIP data can inform corridor risk tools and project scoping. PROTECT Formula project selection is decentralized through districts/ATPs with guidance from RIP and federal requirements.

status: Index-based vulnerability scoring; no single overall formula found
method: Mississippi builds a statewide Vulnerability Index using FEMA NRI and other datasets, plus an Asset Criticality Index. Community vulnerability is scored by inverting BRIC resilience category scores; FEMA NRI hazards use 0-5 risk categories.
inputs: FEMA NRI hazard scores; NOAA/SLOSH flood/storm surge/SLR data; EJScreen/ACS; job and population density; freight network tiers/intermodal connectors; BRIC categories; dam density and hazard class.
scale: FEMA NRI: 5 very high, 4 relatively high, 3 relatively moderate, 2 relatively low, 1 very low, 0 no concern/no data. BRIC six categories: upper half = 0, lower half = 1, summed to community vulnerability 1-5. Dam index weights density and hazard class, with high-hazard dams weighted most.
project: Vulnerability Index and Asset Criticality Index evaluate and rank transportation-system criticality; detailed project prioritization formula not found in selected pages.

status: Explicit multicriteria point scoring
method: NCDOT uses a multicriteria resilience prioritization process to rank vulnerable areas/projects using Criticality Score, Exposure Score, and Sensitivity Score. Only assets on the Criticality Map and exposed to selected hazards are scored.
inputs: Criticality map; exposure to inland flooding, coastal SLR/storm surge, geotechnical hazards; deterministic return periods; probabilistic SLR/CRIS/FEMA NRI annualized frequency; sensitivity by IRI, bridge scour/substructure/channel protection, culvert condition, past washouts.
scale: Low/Medium/High point process; lowest possible score = 3, highest = 12. Exposure and sensitivity are binned L/M/H; high exposure for two hazards + high sensitivity + high criticality reaches 12.
project: STIP projects on the Criticality Map and exposed to hazards are included in prioritization; ranked areas/projects guide resilience investments.

status: Explicit matrix + hotspot ranking
method: NMDOT assigns resilience risk to highway segments <=0.1 mile using exposure, sensitivity, and criticality. Scores are converted to High/Medium/Low by percentile and then combined through criticality-specific matrices into A-D risk classes.
inputs: Exposure; sensitivity; criticality. Freight-network roads/structures automatically receive high criticality. Future exposure adjustment factors are used for wildfire, floods, and drought.
scale: A = Low, B = Medium, C = High, D = Very High. Exposure/sensitivity/criticality High = 75-100%, Medium = 50-74.9%, Low = 0-49.9%. Hotspot adjusted risk = adjusted exposure score x sensitivity score x criticality score; future exposure adjustment capped at +/-25%.
project: High/very-high segments are aggregated into hotspots; hotspots ranked statewide and by district using length-weighted average adjusted resilience risk.

status: Explicit annual risk-cost model
method: ODOT quantifies average annual cost of risk (?risk value?) for flooding, landslides, and rockfalls at asset level, then rolls it up to corridor/district/state scales.
inputs: Threat likelihood/annual closure probability; hazard-specific closure duration/damage assumptions; owner repair/replacement costs; user disruption/detour costs; asset size; landslide susceptibility/history; rockfall inventory; pavement/bridge condition.
scale: Risk value is monetary annualized cost. Example likelihoods include flooding no-damage, flooding damage = flood likelihood x damage likelihood, landslide annual likelihood by susceptibility zone, rockfall likelihood by inventory tier.
project: Priority resilience projects were developed using risk-based vulnerability assessment results plus district/headquarters staff input; social/economic considerations appear through detour length and critical-site input.

status: Explicit 1-5 exposure/consequence matrix
method: ODOT evaluates risk as a function of exposure and consequences. A desktop indicator approach scores exposure and consequence indicators from 1-5 and combines them into corridor-level risk scores by hazard and as multi-hazard risk.
inputs: Exposure to nine climate hazards; consequences from functional class, AADT/traffic flow, and truck flow; historical hazards; future climate; social disparity and asset condition for resilience corridor tiering.
scale: Exposure and consequence each 1-5; final risk matrix ranges 1.0-5.0 using average exposure/consequence. Final scores are classified with Jenks natural breaks into low, medium, high, very high.
project: Resilience Corridors are tiered using climate change, social disparity, and travel disruption potential; ODOT priority corridors with higher truck/traffic flows receive preference.

status: Explicit criticality weights + VAST vulnerability + risk matrix
method: RIDOT uses a criticality score, VAST vulnerability assessment, then incorporates risk by combining event likelihood/probability and impacts/consequences with asset vulnerability.
inputs: Criticality: usage/operational importance, socioeconomic importance, health/safety importance. Vulnerability: exposure, sensitivity, adaptive capacity across asset classes. Risk: likelihood of SLR/storm surge/inland flooding and asset-level vulnerability/consequence.
scale: Criticality Score = Usage & Operational Importance 60% + Socioeconomic Importance 20% + Health & Safety Importance 20%, then percentile categories High/Medium/Low. VAST asset indicators commonly scored 1-4. Risk/criticality matrix identifies acceptable level of change by year.
project: Project managers review criticality, vulnerability, and risk maps for 2035/2050/2100; when risk meets/exceeds acceptable change, it drives resilience need and timeline urgency.

status: Relative vulnerability scoring; no numeric formula in main STRP
method: TxDOT?s asset-based vulnerability assessment rates relative vulnerability from minimal to high. Vulnerability combines exposure and sensitivity: exposure is whether assets are in areas subject to disruptors; sensitivity is the degree of damage after exposure.
inputs: Exposure from geospatial overlays of assets with extreme-weather/disruptor projections; sensitivity by asset type/material/condition; evacuation-route status; disruptors include flooding, hurricanes, SLR/storm surge, extreme heat/cold, wildfire, drought, cyberattacks for ITS/ports/airports.
scale: Relative categories minimal-to-high; high vulnerability counts by asset type and district. Numeric scoring formula not published in extracted main-plan text.
project: Evacuation-route status used to prioritize assets for strategy development; resilience strategies intended to enter standard UTP/project selection; performance measures track damaged critical assets, pavement buckles, alternate routes, evacuation route condition.

status: Explicit asset risk + project prioritization formula
method: UDOT combines normalized exposure and criticality into resilience risk, then combines candidate-project resilience risk with project efficacy scoring for PROTECT prioritization.
inputs: Exposure score; criticality criteria: system redundancy, AADT, truck AADT, disadvantaged community index, proximity to community assets, transit/bike service; project efficacy rubric from region/division staff.
scale: Criticality criteria normalized 1-4 and summed equally. Resilience risk combines exposure and criticality and is converted to Low Risk through Very High Risk using Jenks natural breaks. Candidate project risk uses length-weighted average asset-segment risk as preferred basis; project efficacy normalized 1-100; combined score = (project resilience risk + normalized project efficacy) / 2 with equal weights.
project: Projects are ranked by combined resilience risk and efficacy score. Highest-segment risk is also provided as a flag, but length-weighted average is the basis for prioritization.

status: Framework planned; weights not finalized
method: VDOT plans a risk-based screening approach using exposure, sensitivity, and criticality. Overall vulnerability will be determined by assigning weights/percentages to those three elements.
inputs: Exposure to SLR, storm surge, inland/riverine flooding and future hazards; sensitivity based on asset condition; criticality based on AADT, roadway designation, redundancy, primary evacuation route/important infrastructure.
scale: No final weights or numeric scoring scale published in the downloaded plan; methodology is to be developed and integrated into business practices.
project: VDOT may integrate vulnerability measures into funding programs such as State of Good Repair and SMART SCALE. Resilience measures can be evaluated through multi-criteria analysis with weighted criteria and cost-effectiveness analysis.

status: Draft screening/prioritization only; not full risk model
method: Downloaded VTrans file is a RIP process slide deck. It proposes screening potential projects with yes/no measures and a draft prioritization scan.
inputs: High-risk/documented repeat damage location; redundancy for functional class 1-3 roads/transit/rail; high social vulnerability access; freight access/mode options; coordination with other state resilience/risk plans; natural systems resilience; highly vulnerable/highly critical/in design/ready to build.
scale: Draft prioritization uses Yes=1 for listed flags and sums them. No asset-level risk scoring formula found.
project: Screening is intended to coordinate with Vermont Project Selection and Prioritization (VPSP2) and use TRPT/Capital Program contents.
